title: Entities, attributes, and keys in ER

blocks.text: An **entity** is a distinguishable real-world object or concept (Student, Flight, Course). An **attribute** is a property of an entity (name, seat_no). A **key attribute** uniquely identifies an entity set (roll_no). Composite attributes have parts; derived attributes are computed (age from dob).

ER modelling is casting, not accounting: decide *who* exists in your story (entities), *what you know* about them (attributes), and *how they relate* (relationships) — before a single table exists. The relational schema is a translation of this story, and the mapping rules decide how faithfully it survives.

`Student(roll_no, name, dept)` — roll_no is the key attribute; the entity set maps to a relation with roll_no as its primary key. A weak entity (Dependent) has no key of its own and needs its owner entity plus a partial key.

blocks.prompt: Sanity-check your modelling reflex with a quick verified problem before moving to relationships.
